identity.title: Substrate coupling and inhibition in human Na(+)-dependent Cl(-)/HCO(3)(-) exchanger NCBE (SLC4A10).

content.abstract: Maintaining pH homoeostasis is essential for neuronal excitability and for regulating cerebrospinal fluid (CSF). The Na(+)-dependent Cl(-)/HCO(3)(-) exchanger, NCBE (SLC4A10), abundant in the choroid plexus, contributes to CSF pH control by mediating bicarbonate flux, yet its molecular mechanism has remained unclear. Here we report cryo-EM structures of human NCBE in multiple functional states, revealing conserved binding sites for Na(+), Cl(-), and HCO(3)(-), as well as an unexpected K(+) site indicating relaxed cation selectivity. The inhibitor DIDS binds above the substrate cavity, locking NCBE in an outward-facing conformation and defining a subfamily-selective inhibitory mechanism. Functional assays and molecular dynamics simulations support the coordination of ions and the inhibitory effects. Comparison with an AlphaFold3-predicted inward-facing model suggests an elevator-like transport mechanism and delineates the conformational transitions in Na(+)-dependent HCO(3)(-) transporters. Together, these findings establish a structural framework for NCBE and offer insights into ion coupling and pharmacological modulation within the SLC4 family.
